title: DevEx SDK Guides & Quickstarts — Docs Ops and Top Issues (2026)
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview

This page documents the standard templates, publishing workflow, operational procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues we see from integrators. It is intended for DevEx authors, technical writers, SDK maintainers, solutions engineers, and on-call support.

Goals

- Make SDK guides and quickstarts easy to discover, consistent, and low-maintenance.
- Reduce first-touch support time by surfacing canonical fixes and reproducible API examples.
- Provide an auditable, repeatable publishing workflow with CI checks, reviewers, and rollbacks.

Audience and scope

- Primary: SDK engineers and DevEx writers who author SDK guides, quickstarts, and API examples.
- Secondary: Solutions engineers, support agents, and customers referencing examples.
- Scope: All public and internal SDK docs for Redwood API (hosted, dedicated, private), example apps, and site-level operating procedures for docs publish/maintenance.

Ownership

- Documents and templates: DevEx team (owner team: engineering).
- Docs site CI and linting: eng-developer-experience / platform infra.
- Support canonicals: DevEx + Support rotation owner.

Structure and templates

1) SDK Guide template (use for all language SDKs)

- Title: [SDK] Quickstart: <language> client for Redwood API
- Short intro: 2-3 sentences describing use case and prerequisites (API key, account).
- Prerequisites: OS, package manager, API key scope, required model(s).
- Install: single command to install package.
- Auth: code snippet showing environment variable or config.
- Minimal example: copy-paste code that does one complete request and prints response.
- Error handling: common exceptions and recommended handling pattern.
- Reference: link to SDK reference, rate limits, and model catalog.
- Test matrix: supported SDK versions, supported Node/Python/Java versions.

Snippet (Python minimal example):

```
# Install: pip install redwood-sdk
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-1-large', prompt='Translate to French: Hello world')
print(resp.text)
```

2) Quickstart template (used for single-file quickstarts)

- Goal: what the quickstart accomplishes in one sentence.
- Duration: expected time to complete.
- Prereqs: API key, Node v18+, or Python 3.10+.
- Steps: numbered step-by-step with expected command outputs.
- Validation: how to confirm the quickstart worked (example request and sample response).
- Next steps: links to deeper guides.

3) API examples style guide

- Keep examples minimal and copy-paste runnable.
- Provide idiomatic code for each language we officially support (Python, Node, Go, Java).
- Include both synchronous and streaming examples when applicable.
- Always show authentication and model selection.
- Provide cURL example for quick reproduction.

cURL example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/text/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","prompt":"Summarize the following text..."}'
```

Docs site operating procedures

A) Authoring and branching

1. Create a feature branch named docs/<area>/<short-description> (e.g. docs/sdk/python-streaming).
2. Add or update page using the standard template. Include front-matter: title, summary (1 line), tags, api_surface (sdk|api|examples), last_editor.
3. Run local preview (hugo dev or docs-site dev server) and static checks.

B) CI checks (always run)

- Front-matter check: required fields present.
- Markdown lint: spelling, style.
- Code snippet lint: run language-specific linters where CI supports it.
- Link checker: no 4xx links.
- Size check: flag very large code samples ( > 200 lines ).

C) Review and publishing workflow

- Assign at least one DevEx reviewer and one SDK owner. Reviewers should confirm: correctness, security (no secrets), and reproducibility.
- For API changes: include compatibility note and add deprecation plan if applicable.
- Merge policy: at least 2 approvals required for public-facing changes; 1 approval for internal docs.
- Publishing cadence: changes merged to main trigger a deploy to staging; manual promotion to production after smoke tests.

D) Rollback and hotfixes

- If a publishing issue is found in prod, open a docs incident, revert the offending commit, and patch branch with corrected content.
- Communicate incident to #devex and #support with CHANGE_ID and summary.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (most frequent)

Below are the top recurring issues we observe and the canonical fixes or guidance to include in docs. When an issue is added, update this list and the corresponding quickstart or SDK guide.

1) Authentication: invalid or missing API key
- Symptom: 401 response with message "invalid_api_key".
- Root cause: user configured REDWOOD_API_KEY incorrectly or used read-only key for write operations.
- Canonical fix: show how to create a new key, scope guidance, and example of exporting to env (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...). Add a retry note for transient 401s after rotation.

2) Rate limiting and 429s
- Symptom: 429 responses during burst traffic.
- Root cause: default rate limits for free tiers or misconfigured client concurrency.
- Canonical fix: recommend exponential backoff with jitter, link to per-account rate limit dashboard, and quick config for client-side concurrency.

3) Streaming disconnects in unreliable networks
- Symptom: partial streaming response or broken pipe errors.
- Root cause: network interruptions or overly long keepalive timeouts in proxies.
- Canonical fix: provide reconnect patterns, idempotency guidance, and example using chunked streaming with explicit resume tokens where supported.

4) Model selection mismatches / mismatched max_tokens
- Symptom: truncated output or high latency when requesting long sequences.
- Root cause: mismatch between model capability and requested max_tokens / context window.
- Canonical fix: add model recommendation table and example to detect and fall back to compatible model variants.

5) Dependency and install failures
- Symptom: failing pip/npm installs due to mismatched versions.
- Root cause: local environment mismatch (Python version or locked dependency).
- Canonical fix: include explicit supported versions, reproducible virtualenv/venv commands, and Docker quickstart with pinned package versions.

6) Unexpected JSON/serialization errors
- Symptom: SDK throws serialization or validation errors for request body.
- Root cause: users passing non-serializable objects (datetime, bytes) or wrong content-type header.
- Canonical fix: add helper utilities in SDK docs to sanitize payloads and example server-side validation code.

7) Private deployment networking (VPC) connectivity issues
- Symptom: connection timeouts when using private control plane.
- Root cause: missing routing rules, NAT, or incorrect TLS termination.
- Canonical fix: include network checklist for on-prem and VPC customers: required ports, proxy timeouts, TLS cert locations, and sample iptables / security group rules.

8) Tokenization and cost surprises
- Symptom: customer reports higher cost due to unexpected tokenization.
- Root cause: prompt format, hidden whitespace, or unsupported encoding.
- Canonical fix: include token counting examples, recommended prompt templates, and tips to reduce accidental verbosity.

Triage playbook for incoming docs/support issues

1. Reproduce: ask for minimal reproduction (code snippet, request id, timestamp).
2. Identify: check request id in logs, map to infra trace, determine surface area (SDK, API, docs).
3. Fix: if docs-related, prepare quick PR against the relevant quickstart or SDK guide. Use the hotfix branch docs/hotfix/<short-desc>.
4. Communicate: post summary and link to PR/incident in #devex and #support.

Metrics and SLAs for docs health

- Documentation coverage: percent of SDK endpoints with at least one example (goal: 95%).
- Reproducibility score: percent of examples that pass CI-run smoke test (goal: 90%+).
- Mean time to first-response for docs-supported tickets: < 8 hours during business hours.
- Broken-link rate: < 0.5% of pages monthly.

Maintenance checklist (monthly)

- Run site link-checker and fix broken links.
- Run code-snippet smoke tests for all official languages.
- Review top 10 search queries and add quickstarts for high-intent queries.
- Audit examples for security (no secrets, no internal endpoints).
- Update model recommendations table with recent performance/price changes.

Appendix: recommended frontmatter and lint rules

Frontmatter fields (required):
- title
- summary
- tags (list)
- api_surface: sdk|api|examples
- last_editor
- sdk_language (if applicable)

CI lint rules (high level):
- enforce code-block language labels (```python, ```bash, etc.).
- forbid inline secrets (regex detect patterns like "AKIA|sk-" etc.).
- require reproducible example (single file) for quickstarts.

Appendix: small debugging checklist for support agents

- Verify API key in headers matches account and scopes.
- If 429: check per-key/concurrency rate, advise backoff.
- If 401: ask for rotated key timing and recommend clearing caches.
- For private deployments: confirm customer control-plane certificate validity and IP allowlist.

Change history

- 2026-03-15: Initial draft by Sofia Martinez.
- 2026-03-22: Reviewer feedback incorporated (Ethan Chen, Priya Nair).
- 2026-04-02: Published after CI smoke tests; added triage playbook (Liam O'Connor).

If you are updating these templates: update the front-matter in the page, link to any SDK repo changes, and run the docs CI. For questions or to request a new quickstart, open a PR or raise a topic in #devex.
